items.stem: In one line: why is discount calculated on the marked price but profit on the cost price?
items.answer: Discount is a reduction offered from the price displayed (MP); profit is the gain compared with what the seller paid (CP).
items.markingKey: Discount is a reduction offered from the price displayed (MP); profit is the gain compared with what the seller paid (CP).

items.stem: A student says: 'Sold for ₹100 at 20% profit, so the cost price was ₹80.' Is this right?
items.answer: No: CP = 100 ÷ 1.20 = ₹83.33. Twenty percent of CP, not of SP, is the profit.
items.markingKey: No: CP = 100 ÷ 1.20 = ₹83.33. Twenty percent of CP, not of SP, is the profit.
